question: What does the source's stated 6×5 fractionation grid actually evaluate on its six intended LP2 pages, and does its columnar reversal invert the stated transform?
target_mapping: Source historical P21,22,23,27,28,30 are LP2-21,22,23,27,28,30, now pinned global scan folders 38,39,40,44,45,47. Current bare page_21 etc are different pages.
alphabet: GP indices 0..28, 6×5 row-major table with cell (5,4) unused; source keyword-first deduplicated alphabet
source_gate: score_plain >20 OR raw IoC >1.3. Keep invalid defractionated cells as -1 exactly as source does; source IoC counts them as one repeated symbol. Report invalid count separately and never treat this gate as a decode verdict.
corrected_variant: For each of the same seven widths only, invert the source's columnar_transpose exactly using natural column order and actual per-column lengths. This is a separate named variant, never substituted for a source result. Retain all 14 keys and six targets.
controls: Before manuscript scoring, use deterministic known GP messages at each of the six target lengths, every keyword and every seven widths: fractionate, columnar_transpose, then require corrected inverse plus defractionate to recover the exact full message. Measure source inverse failures on those same planted streams; direct table inversion must recover all 29 symbols. Independently compare source and local table, parser, split and score on source-pinned examples.
scope_note: The source's four other split points return fewer than n pairs and are skipped by its own length condition; preserve named skipped rows. The P08 running-key and solved-page running-key bonus blocks are different experiments and excluded from this fractionation grid.
exclusions: Other widths, table keys, page ranges, keyed column orders, cipher-level encodings of coordinate streams, null handling other than source's -1, and any claim that high source score or raw IoC identifies a plaintext.
